latin.529: §. IX. Testimonia SECULI QUINTI, seu postremi eorum, quibus de puriori doctrina Evangelica gloriari datum est, etsi ex pluribus Patribus tàm Græcis, quam Latinis, Theodoreto, Cyrillo, Prospero Aquitanico, Fulgentio aliisque colligi adducique possent uberrima, nobis tamen hôc locô suffecerit in duorum, diffusioris cùm eruditionis, tùm Commentationis atque eloquii sacri, palmam, & Antecessoribus, & Successoribus, facilè præripientium Patrum Sententiis acquievisse. Alter horum Orientalis, Occidentalis Ecclesiæ alter Doctor kat' exochēn communisque & meretur dici, & vulgò consuevit appellari, S. CHRYSOSTOMUM intelligo, & S. AUGUSTINUM.
latin.530: PRIOR uti à Mysteriis omnibus Carnalitatem, sic à S. Cœna, corporis Christi carnalem tùm præsentiam, tùm participationem, semoturus, Homil. 45. in Johannem ita commentatur: Mysteria, inquit, non sunt carnaliter, sed interioribus oculis, i. e. spiritualiter, consideranda & contemplanda; Hujusmodi enim est Mysteriorum natura. Et paucis interjectis, sic pergit: Sicut in Baptismo, sensibili aqua elemento, intelligibile Regenerationis donum; ita etiam INTELLIGIBILE hoc corporis & sanguinis Christi donum, non corporea aut sensibili aliquâ actione, sed spirituali fidei intelligentiâ, animo atque mente percipitur.
latin.531: POSTERIOR verò, Veritatem in hoc puncto divinam omnem elocuturus (1) Verba Institutionis S. Cœnæ Essentialia: Accipite edite, Hoc est Corpus meum, figurata esse, nec sine Metonymiæ tropo accipienda, satis clarè pronuntiat, quando contra Adimantum Lib. 12. ita scribit: Dominus non dubitavit dicere, Hoc est corpus meum, cum signum daret corporis sui, subnexa insuper ratione Lib. 2. de Doctrina Christ. c. 16., ob quam in mandato Christi, de manducando corpore suo, aliisque similibus, Figura necessariò subintelligenda sit; si, inquit Augustinus, præceptiva locutio aut flagitium aut facinus videtur jubere, aut utilitatem aut beneficium vetare, figurata est. Nisi manducaveritis, inquit Christus, carnem Filii Hominis & sanguinem biberitis, non habebitis Vitam in vobis, facinus vel flagitium videtur jubere, FIGURA EST ERGO, præcipiens, Passioni Domini esse communicandum & suaviter atque utiliter recondendum in memoria, quod pro nobis caro ejus crucifixa & vulnerata est.
latin.532: (2) Figuratam interim Christi locutionem, veram corporis ejus in Cœna S., vel præsentiam, vel participationem, neutiquam è medio tollere dicit: Jam, ait Augustinus, Christiani, peracti sacrificii memoriam, celebrant, sacrosanctâ oblatione & participatione Corporis & sanguinis Christi, Lib. 20. contra Faustum cap. 18. confer. cap. 21. At verò (3.) Præsentiam atque participationem Corporis Christi in Cœna, Spirituales facit: Spiritualiter inquit, intelligite quæ locutus sum (Christum hic loquentem introducens); Nam hoc Corpus, quod videtis, manducaturi estis & bibituri illum sanguinem, quem fusuri sunt, qui me crucifigent, Sacramentum vobis aliquod commendavi, SPIRITUALITER intellectum vivificabit vos in Psalm. 98. Item Tractatu 25. in Johannem: Ut quid paras dentes & Ventrem: Crede & manducasti.
latin.533: Idque (4.) cum exclusione præsentiæ localis & participationis oralis: Ita enim Tract. 30. in Johannem pergit: Donec seculum finiatur, sursum est Dominus, sed tamen, hic etiam nobiscum est Veritas Domini. CORPUS ENIM DOMINI, IN QUO RESURREXIT, UNO LOCO esse oportet, veritas autem ejus ubique diffusa est. Et Tract. 50. in Johann. Christus absens etiam præsens est: Corpus enim suum intulit cœlo, Majestatem non abstulit mundo. Et Tract. I. in Epistolam Johannis. Dominum jam in cælo sedentem MANU (ore) contrectare non possumus, sed Fide contingere.
latin.534: Etiam (5) cum exclusione participationis Corporis Christi, quod ad indignos, i. e. Impœnitentes atq; incredulos attinet. Sic enim expressè discriminat inter manducationem credentium Christi Discipulorum, & Judæ proditoris Christi: Discipuli, ait, manducabant panem Dominum; Judas panem Domini, contra Dominum, Tract. 59. in Johannem.

pass_a.529: §. IX. The Testimonies of the FIFTH age — or the last of those to which it was given to glory in the purer Evangelical doctrine — although most abundant ones could be gathered and brought from more Fathers both Greek and Latin, Theodoret, Cyril, Prosper of Aquitaine, Fulgentius and others, yet it will suffice us in this place to have rested in the Sentences of two Fathers who easily snatch the palm of both broader learning and sacred Commentary and eloquence from Predecessors and Successors. One of these the Doctor par excellence of the Eastern, the other of the Western Church, and common, both deserves to be called and is commonly wont to be called — I mean S. CHRYSOSTOM and S. AUGUSTINE.
pass_a.530: The FORMER, about to remove Carnality from all Mysteries, and so from the Sacred Supper both the carnal presence and the participation of Christ’s body, comments thus in Homily 45 on John: Mysteries, he says, are not to be considered and contemplated carnally, but with interior eyes, i.e. spiritually; For such is the nature of Mysteries. And a few words interposed, he proceeds thus: As in Baptism, by the sensible element water, the intelligible gift of Regeneration; so also this INTELLIGIBLE gift of Christ’s body and blood is perceived not by any corporeal or sensible action, but by the spiritual intelligence of faith, with soul and mind.
pass_a.531: But the LATTER, about to utter every divine Truth on this point, (1) pronounces clearly enough that the Essential Institution words of the Sacred Supper — Take, eat, This is my Body — are figurative and not to be received without the trope of Metonymy, when against Adimantus Book 12 he writes thus: The Lord did not hesitate to say, This is my body, when He was giving a sign of His body, with reason further annexed in Book 2 On Christian Doctrine ch. 16, on account of which in Christ’s command about eating His body and in similar sayings a Figure must necessarily be understood underneath; if, says Augustine, a preceptive utterance seems to order a crime or outrage, or to forbid a usefulness or benefit, it is figurative. Unless you shall have eaten, says Christ, the flesh of the Son of Man and drunk His blood, you will not have Life in you — it seems to order a crime or outrage; IT IS THEREFORE A FIGURE, commanding that one must communicate in the Lord’s Passion and sweetly and usefully lay up in memory that His flesh was crucified and wounded for us.
pass_a.532: (2) Meanwhile he says the figurative speech of Christ by no means removes from the midst the true presence or participation of His body in the Sacred Supper: Already, says Augustine, Christians celebrate the memory of the sacrifice accomplished, with sacrosanct oblation and participation of the Body and blood of Christ (Against Faustus Book 20 ch. 18, compare ch. 21). But (3.) He makes the Presence and participation of Christ’s Body in the Supper Spiritual: Spiritually, he says, understand what I have spoken (introducing Christ speaking here); For this Body which you see you are about to eat and drink that blood which they will shed who will crucify me — I have committed to you a certain Sacrament; understood SPIRITUALLY it will quicken you (Psalm 98). Also Tractate 25 on John: Why prepare teeth and Belly: Believe and you have eaten.
pass_a.533: And that (4.) with exclusion of local presence and oral participation: For so he proceeds in Tract. 30 on John: Until the age is finished, the Lord is above, yet nonetheless here also with us is the Truth of the Lord. FOR THE BODY OF THE LORD, IN WHICH HE ROSE, ought to be IN ONE PLACE, but His truth is diffused everywhere. And Tract. 50 on John: Christ even when absent is present: For He has brought His body into heaven, He has not withdrawn His Majesty from the world. And Tract. I on the Epistle of John: We cannot handle with HAND (mouth) the Lord now sitting in heaven, but touch by Faith.
pass_a.534: Also (5) with exclusion of participation of Christ’s Body as concerns the unworthy, i.e. the Impenitent and unbelieving. For so he expressly discriminates between the eating of Christ’s believing Disciples and of Judas the traitor of Christ: The Disciples, he says, were eating the bread the Lord; Judas the bread of the Lord, against the Lord (Tract. 59 on John).

529: §.IX: for the FIFTH century — last of the purer Evangelical ages — many Fathers could be cited, but two snatch the palm.
East and West’s doctors par excellence: Chrysostom and Augustine.
530: Chrysostom (Hom. 45 on John) strips carnality from the mysteries and from the Supper’s carnal presence and participation.

Mysteries are for interior eyes — spiritual. As baptism’s sensible water carries an intelligible regeneration-gift, so the intelligible gift of body and blood is received by faith’s spiritual intelligence, not by bodily action.
531: Augustine (1): the essential Institution words (‘Take, eat, This is my Body’) are figurative — not without metonymy (Against Adimantus 12; Doctr. Chr. 2.16).
If a command seems to order a crime, it is figurative: ‘Unless you eat my flesh…’ seems criminal — therefore it is a FIGURE commanding communion in the Passion and memory of the crucified flesh.
532: Augustine (2): the figure does not remove true presence or participation — Christians celebrate with sacrosanct oblation and participation of Body and blood (Against Faustus 20.18).
(3) Presence and participation are spiritual: understand spiritually; the sacrament understood spiritually quickens (Ps. 98). Tract. 25 John: Why prepare teeth and belly? Believe, and you have eaten.
533: Augustine (4): local presence and oral handling shut out — until the age ends the Lord is above, yet His Truth is here with us.

The Lord’s risen body must be in ONE PLACE; His truth is everywhere. Absent yet present: body in heaven, Majesty not withdrawn. We cannot handle Him in heaven with hand or mouth — only touch by Faith.
534: Augustine (5): the unworthy (impenitent, unbelieving) are excluded from participation of the Body.
Disciples ate the bread the Lord; Judas ate the Lord’s bread against the Lord (Tract. 59 on John).
Stop before §.X (sixth century onward — decline; Gelasius still holding).

notes.533: Augustine (4): one place; faith not mouth.
